headline: Dataset is clean and safe to train on — all exact checks pass; the only flags are experimental-detector false positives from normal class-boundary ambiguity.
training_impact: Trains without issue. No missing/orphan/empty labels, no malformed rows, no corrupt images, no out-of-bounds/degenerate/tiny/duplicate boxes, coordinates are properly normalised, all class ids are in range, and there is no train/val leakage or near-duplicate content. The validation number will be meaningful. The only real (minor) caveat is genuine label ambiguity on a handful of car/truck and cup/bowl boxes, which will add a little noise to those two class pairs but will not corrupt the run or the metric.

decisions.rationale: 37 truck→car, but only 37/201 of train trucks, and it is paired with the reverse car→truck finding (6 boxes). Two-way, small-fraction disagreement is the signature of car/truck boundary ambiguity (pickups, partial occlusion), not a one-directional mapping bug. Experimental detector, so not a finding on its own. [verifier upheld: The evidence shows a two-way disagreement (37 truck-to-car vs 6 car-to-truck) between visually similar classes, which is the specific signature of annotation ambiguity rather than a systematic defect.]

6 car→truck, 6/577 of train cars, and the mirror of the truck→car finding. Bidirectional pair = ordinary ambiguity, not a systematic remap error. [verifier upheld: The evidence shows a bidirectional disagreement between visually similar classes (car and truck), which indicates annotation ambiguity rather than a systematic defect.]

7 cup→bowl, 7/355 of train cups, paired with the reverse bowl→cup finding (4 boxes). Two-way, small-fraction = deep-mug-vs-bowl ambiguity, not a mapping bug. [verifier upheld: The evidence shows a two-way disagreement between visually similar classes (cup and bowl) in a small fraction of the dataset, which indicates annotation ambiguity rather than a systematic defect.]

4 bowl→cup, 4/251 of train bowls, mirror of the cup→bowl finding. Bidirectional pair = boundary ambiguity, not a real defect. [verifier upheld: The evidence shows a bidirectional disagreement between visually similar classes ('bowl' and 'cup'), which indicates annotation ambiguity rather than a systematic defect.]

2 boxes (1 train, 1 val), handbag↔backpack — a classic COCO confusion pair. 2/274 handbags is scattered disagreement, not a systematic error.
